Token Generation Predictability [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-331] on TokenGenerationLambda, SecretsManager, DynamoDB: If tokens are generated using predictable patterns or weak cryptographic methods, attackers could analyze the token format and generation patterns to predict or generate valid tokens. An attacker captures multiple valid tokens, analyzes their pattern, and creates a script to generate valid tokens, bypassing the queue system.

Queue State Manipulation [Tampering, Denial of Service, CWE-841] on Redis, QueueManagementLambda, CounterManagementLambda, DynamoDB: If access controls to Redis or DynamoDB are not properly configured, or if there are injection vulnerabilities in the queue management logic, an attacker could modify queue state data. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the queue management API to modify queue positions or counter values, causing legitimate users to experience extremely long wait times.

Private API Endpoint Exposure [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-548] on PrivateApi, CounterManagementLambda, SessionManagementLambda: Private API endpoints could be exposed through misconfigured network settings, logging of sensitive information, or through DNS enumeration techniques. An attacker discovers private API endpoints through leaked logs or network scanning, then attempts to access administrative functions.

Token Storage and Session Management Vulnerabilities [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, CWE-384] on TokenGenerationLambda, SessionManagementLambda, SecretsManager, DynamoDB: Improper token storage, lack of expiration mechanisms, or weak session management could allow tokens to be stolen, reused, or remain valid indefinitely. An attacker captures a valid token and reuses it multiple times to bypass the queue, or uses an expired token that hasn't been properly invalidated.

Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on CloudFront, APIGateway, Lambda, Redis, DynamoDB: Attackers could send a large volume of requests to overwhelm the system's capacity, particularly targeting the queue management and token generation endpoints. An attacker uses a botnet to generate thousands of queue requests per second, overwhelming the system and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service.
